name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

areaKm2.note: LoN Statistical Year-Book 1938/39 Table 2: United Kingdom 244 thousand km2 (incl. Northern Ireland 14). The world_1938 'United Kingdom' feature (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1938.geojson) also contains Cyprus (~9,200 km2); without it the GB+NI polygons are ~218,800 km2 on the sphere (coarse coastline), used as low.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1939 = 47,762k (UK incl. Northern Ireland); LoN Statistical Year-Book 1938/39 Table 2 gives 47,485k for June 1938 (low side); COW 1940 = 48,226k (high).

urbanization.note: HYDE via OWID: United Kingdom 1940 = 75.6% urban (mid). Low = COW upop/tpop 1939 = 18,429/47,762 = 0.386 (cities over 100,000 only).

activePersonnel.note: Army 892,697 regulars + Territorial Army at the outbreak (French 2000 pp. 63-64; Crang 2000 gives 1,065,000 for 3 Sep 1939, used in high) + Royal Navy ~200,000 incl. Royal Marines and reserves (naval-history.net) + RAF 175,392 (Sep 1939, Wynn 1976 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personnel_numbers_in_the_Royal_Air_Force). COW milper 1939 = 394k and Harrison Table 1-5 = 480k are pre-mobilisation annual figures, so they are not used.

trainedReserves.note: Regular Army Reserve 173,700 (only ~3,700 fully trained per French 2000) plus TA reserve ~20,750 (April 1939); RN and RAF reserves are already inside the active figures. The Militia (conscripts of May 1939, 20-21 year olds) were in training.

supportPersonnel.note: active minus P roles: RN ~200,000, RAF ~175,000, and the army's artillery, armoured, engineer, signals, RASC and AA (TA AA divisions) troops, depots and staffs.

mobilizationRatio.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-5: UK armed forces peaked at 5,090k (1945), i.e. 0.106 of ~48M. High allows for the ~5.9M who served at some point (turnover); that total is from general literature, not the fetched table.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Reconstruction: ~140 regular infantry battalions (many in India, Palestine, Egypt) at ~700 plus ~200 Territorial battalions of the 12 first-line and 12 duplicate TA divisions at ~550 (TA doubled in March 1939, many under strength). 8 regular + 12 first-line TA infantry divisions (French 2000).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: SMLE rifle and Bren gun good; 2-pdr AT guns and Boys rifles scarce; only 78 25-pdrs delivered (Pemberton p. 27)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: long-service regulars professional; doubled TA and the May 1939 Militia had weeks of training

count.note: Educated guess: the regular cavalry was largely mechanised by 1939 (~30 cavalry or armoured regiments in total); still-horsed yeomanry regiments formed the 1st Cavalry Division (sent to Palestine early 1940). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army_during_the_Second_World_War)

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: horsed yeomanry with rifles, obsolete for European war

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: Territorial yeomanry

count.note: Postan, British War Production (HMSO 1952) p. 103 via the cited page: 969 tanks produced in 1939 (734 light, 235 I-tank/cruiser) of the Oct 1938-June 1940 programme; with older Mk II-V lights in Egypt and India roughly 1,000 on hand. The BEF and 1st Armoured Division had few cruiser/infantry tanks (~200 by Oct 1939). Grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mostly Mk VI light tanks with machine guns; Matilda I MG-only; only 2 Matilda II at outbreak

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Royal Tank Corps professional cadre, newly mechanised cavalry

count.note: Educated guess anchored on ~1,000 field guns and 600 anti-tank guns abandoned in France in June 1940 (the BEF had ~10 divisions); field and medium guns at home and overseas, largely WWI 18-pdr and 4.5-in stocks plus 78 25-pdrs. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army_during_the_Second_World_War)

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: WWI-vintage 18-pdr and 6-in howitzers converting to the 25-pdr

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Royal Artillery gunnery professional; fire control and survey strong

count.note: Batteries. Collier, Defence of the United Kingdom ch. IV: 570 heavy AA guns and ~2,000 searchlights ready for deployment by spring 1939; light AA very scarce (the 1939 plan's 2,000 light barrels not yet delivered). ~600-700 heavy guns at 4 per battery plus a few light batteries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: 3.7-in heavy AA gun among the best of the era; Bofors light guns only arriving

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: manned by Territorial AA divisions

count.note: Richards, RAF 1939-45 vol. I ch. III: Fighter Command had 35 squadrons in Sep 1939 (22 with Hurricanes and Spitfires) plus 4 sent to France; at 16 initial-equipment aircraft per squadron ~620-690, plus a few overseas Gladiator squadrons and FAA Skuas. Immediate reserve of 4-5 per squadron excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Spitfire I and Hurricane I comparable to the Bf 109E; rest Gladiator biplanes and Blenheim IF

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service RAF pilots, radar-directed interception practised

count.note: Richards vol. I Appendix V: RAF first-line strength 3 Sep 1939 = 1,911 aircraft (establishment, home and overseas). Minus ~650 fighters = ~1,260 bombers, Coastal Command and army co-operation aircraft; plus Fleet Air Arm Swordfish/Skua strike aircraft (~150-200, not in the RAF total).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Wellington, Whitley, Hampden, Blenheim, Battle; Battle obsolete, no heavy bombers yet

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: professional crews but poor night navigation (Richards ch. II)

count.note: Capital ships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers. naval-history.net Sep 1939: 15 battleships/battlecruisers, 7 aircraft carriers, 66 cruisers including Dominion ships; minus 8 Dominion cruisers (RAN 6, NZ Division 2) = 80 for the UK alone (78/80/82, grade A); plus destroyers from the naval-history.net tables (https://www.naval-history.net/WW2aBritishLosses10tables.htm, grade B): 184 in Sep 1939 including Dominion, minus 11 (RAN 5, RCN 6) = 173. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor.

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of capital ships/carriers/cruisers (80) and destroyers (173), both 0.55/0.65/0.75, role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: only 2 capital ships post-WWI (Nelson, Rodney); 5 KGV building; carriers with obsolescent aircraft; over half of destroyers modern; ASDIC and early radar

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of capital ships/carriers/cruisers 0.8/0.85/0.9 (80) and destroyers 0.75/0.8/0.9 (173), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: training 0.75-1.0 and 0.75. Evidence: long-service professional navy, best ship handling of the era

count.note: naval-history.net tables: ~35 of the 45 escort and patrol vessels (sloops; minus 10 Dominion/RIN sloops). Minesweepers and coastal craft excluded. The 173 UK destroyers moved to ships_major (was 200/208/230), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: over half of destroyers modern; few long-range escorts

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional crews

count.note: naval-history.net: 60 submarines in Sep 1939, mostly modern, 9 building; no Dominion submarines.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: T, S and U classes; good boats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional submarine service

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Staff College system and Imperial General Staff; 1940 France and Norway showed slow, rigid army command; Admiralty and Air Ministry staff competent

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: regimental system gave strong unit identity; Territorial units locally recruited

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: no war enthusiasm but broad support after Munich and Prague; hardened in 1940

weapons.note: Anchor: between 7 (1905) and 8 (1943). Evidence: Bren LMG, 3.7-in AA, 25-pdr entering service; most field guns WWI, light tanks MG-armed

armor.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: Matilda II (78 mm armour) existed in 2 units; most tanks thin-skinned lights

ships.note: Anchor: close to 8 (carriers, radar, submarines). Evidence: 7 carriers, ASDIC, first Type 79 radars at sea; capital ships mostly WWI-built

fortification.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8 (Maginot). Evidence: no continental line of its own; coastal batteries and Scapa defences

logistics.note: Anchor: 8 (motor transport + rail). Evidence: BEF was the only fully motorised army of 1939; dense rail network

communications.note: Anchor: 7.5-8. Evidence: wireless in tanks and HQs, no company-level radio yet; Dowding system landlines

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar. Evidence: Chain Home radar network operational along the east and south coasts in 1939; photo reconnaissance audit 2026-10-30: mid 8.0 -> 7.89, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1939 (7.895); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

air.note: Anchor: air 8 = 1943. Evidence: Spitfire, Hurricane, Wellington in service; no four-engine bombers yet

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): United Kingdom 1938 = 9,988, 1939 = 9,982 (2011 int$). Range widened for MPD benchmark uncertainty; the 1940 war-boom value 10,928 is not used.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-8: military outlays 15% of national income in 1939 (current prices), 44% in 1940. Low ~7% approximates 1938 rearmament (educated, not in the table).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry, mining and construction ~40% of UK output in the late 1930s; Harrison 1998 describes the UK as the most industrialised and least self-sufficient great power. (context page: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf)

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - a / s (a = agricultural share of employment, s = calorie self-sufficiency). a: Herrendorf et al. via OWID, United Kingdom agriculture share of employment 1935 = 6.8%, 1937 = 6.1%, 1938 = 5.9%. s: "At the beginning of the war Britain produced 33 percent of the calories its people consumed" (44% by 1945), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeding_Britain_in_the_Second_World_War. Mid 1 - 0.059/0.33 = 0.82. Low a 0.068, s 0.30 = 0.77; high a 0.055, s 0.36 = 0.85. Grade C: two sources combined. Import dependence: two thirds of calories imported (Harrison 1998: Britain relied heavily on imported food and fuels). audit 2026-10-30: was 0.0/0.0/0.02 (read as a trade balance); recomputed with the formula and the fetched s.

annualCohort.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 3(a): males aged 20-24, England and Wales 1,611k (est. June 1937), Scotland 210.2k, Northern Ireland 52.5k (1926) = 1,874k / 5 = ~375k per year.

armor.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: UK tanks and SPG 1941 = 4.8k, 1942 = 8.6k, 1943 = 7.5k, 1944 = 4.6k per year.

aircraft_fighter.note: Harrison Table 1-6: UK combat aircraft 13.2k (1941) to 22.7k (1944); fighters ~40% of output (British Empire fighters 38,786 per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_production_during_World_War_II).

aircraft_strike.note: Harrison Table 1-6 combat aircraft 13.2k-22.7k per year minus fighters (~60% bombers, attack, maritime).

artillery.note: Harrison Table 1-6: UK 'guns' 33k (1941), 106k (1942), 118k (1943); this includes anti-tank, AA and small-calibre cannon, so the mid takes roughly half for ground artillery-type weapons.

ships_major.note: 1939-45 British Empire built 15 fleet carriers, 5 battleships, 35 cruisers (plus 29 escort carriers) per the cited page, ~9 per year.

ships_minor.note: Harrison Table 1-6: UK major naval vessels 236 (1941), 239 (1942), 224 (1943) incl. destroyers, frigates, corvettes and submarines (landing craft excluded); minus submarines.

submarines.note: 238 submarines 1939-45 (British Empire) per the cited page, ~40 per year.

roadKm.note: Maybury (Royal Society of Arts lecture, Commercial Motor 15 Dec 1931): 177,256 miles of highway in Great Britain = 285,000 km; plus Northern Ireland (~21,000 km, educated). Essentially all surfaced.

railKm.note: Big Four route mileage: LMS >7,100, LNER 6,590, GWR 3,800, SR 2,186 = >19,676 miles (>31,600 km), plus London Transport, joint lines and Northern Ireland railways (~1,200 km).

majorPorts.note: London, Liverpool, Clyde/Glasgow, Southampton, Bristol/Avonmouth, Hull, Tyne, Cardiff, Belfast, plus naval bases Portsmouth, Plymouth, Rosyth and Scapa Flow (Home Fleet bases per naval-history.net).

merchantTonnage.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 113 (Lloyd's Register, June 1938): United Kingdom and Ireland 17,781k gross tons (Irish share negligible). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (x1.3-1.6) for a mixed cargo fleet.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War ch. 5-6: motorised supply columns of 1939-41 sustained operations ~300-500 km beyond railheads; the BEF was fully motorised. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: UK national horse stock 1.2M in 1930 (Rich and Wilson p. 653, table 59, via the cited page), declining through the 1930s with mechanisation. The army itself used very few horses.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified naval bases, strong population support; the Channel acts as a moat (high 1.3) though there is no strategic depth or harsh climate.

notes: Snapshot date 3 September 1939 (declaration of war). United Kingdom ONLY: home islands (Great Britain and Northern Ireland). includes is empty: forces, population and GDP of India, the Dominions and the colonies are NOT counted; Dominion warships (RAN, RCN, NZ Division) were subtracted from the naval-history.net totals. Overseas British Army garrisons (India, Egypt, Palestine) and overseas RAF squadrons ARE counted because they were UK forces. The hb:1938:United Kingdom polygon also contains Cyprus; area uses the LoN figure for GB+NI. Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, battlecruisers, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major; sloops (ocean escorts) and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Weakest values: artillery (educated guess), infantry share of the army (reconstruction), roadKm for Northern Ireland, industrialShare. COW NMC v7 (2025 release) used instead of v6; values for these years are unchanged in substance. Merchant tonnage converted from gross to deadweight tons at x1.5.
